subject: Spatially varying correlation in Kronecker product model

messages.author: 7d75f2ec7d93b05e
messages.subject: Spatially varying correlation in Kronecker product model
parts:
Hi all - 

I have two spatial (and temporal but I'm not worrying about that for now) outcomes, Y1 and Y2, which are both observed at every location (on the sphere) in my dataset. I believe that they have similar spatial correlation structures. I also know that the two outcomes are correlated together, but that their correlation is spatially varying.

At the moment, I'm doing some exploratory INLA fitting with SPDE on each outcome univariately, but I'd like to fit the models jointly. If the correlation between Y1 and Y2 was constant in space, I'd use the Kronecker product model tools implemented in INLA with exponential correlation and set my grouping to consist of my two outcomes. 

Is there any way to extend the Kronecker product model to allow for a spatially varying correlation? Possibly something that allows me to use the SPDE tools to build up a finite element approximation to the correlation structure?

much thanks,
Aaron

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatially varying correlation in Kronecker product model
parts:
Hi,

We haven't really explored that kind of model yet, but in principle one could build it with the help of inla.spde2.generic(), which is the internal model translator for the mesh based SPDE models. It would allow at least some types of multivariate nonstationarity of the type you describe, where the two fields would be treated internally as two parts of a single model.  Doing this requires some understanding of the technical aspects of the finite element constructions etc.

Finn L
